raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-UK-PadeswoodCCUS",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Integrating FOAK carbon capture technology at an operational cement plant at scale introduces potential technical integration and performance risks.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Conduct independent technical assurance via third-party experts and enforce strict performance thresholds within the Industrial Carbon Capture contract.",
      "evidence": "Padeswood will be the first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Spurline development delays could force a 4-month delay to Final Investment Decision (FID) and a 5-month delay to Commercial Operation Date (COD).",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Proactively align spurline delivery timelines and project FID milestones via the Cluster Sponsor Function oversight body.",
      "evidence": "FID is delayed by 4 months to align with their spurline timelines, resulting in a subsequent 5-month delay to COD"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Rising carbon prices and exposure to unabated overseas competition risk carbon leakage and loss of market share prior to full CCUS operation.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Deploy Industrial Carbon Capture revenue support contracts to bridge the operating cost gap and maintain market competitiveness.",
      "evidence": "Without CCUS, the cement industry will increasingly be exposed to a rising carbon price, impacting competitiveness with imports."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Internationally owned corporate parent may de-prioritise UK interests and reallocate investment overseas if UK decarbonisation frameworks lag.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Provide long-term policy and commercial certainty through 25-year business model frameworks and Grant Funding Agreements.",
      "evidence": "Most UK cement sites are operated by companies that are internationally owned and make investment decisions on a global basis."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "High upfront capital expenditure during capture facility construction creates risk of cost overruns and funding shortfalls.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide upfront capital support via the CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant up to 50% of eligible costs using an Open Book Model.",
      "evidence": "The CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant, which provides upfront capital support during the construction phase, up to 50% of Padeswood’s eligible capital costs."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Interdependent cross-chain interfaces between the Padeswood capture plant and the broader HyNet T&S network create operational delivery risks.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a dedicated Cluster Sponsor Function to actively manage cross-chain delivery and operating model integration risks.",
      "evidence": "Managing government-owned cross-chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Fluctuations in captured CO2 volumes or operational disruptions create income uncertainty under long-term support contracts.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Structure revenue support under a Contract-for-Difference model tying payments to captured CO2 performance and volume thresholds.",
      "evidence": "address key market barriers facing CCS deployment – such as high upfront costs, cross-chain risks, and revenue uncertainty"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Premature project discontinuation during development or operation could result in major write-downs of public capital and unfulfilled carbon targets.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Enforce Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and continuous compliance monitoring by LCCC and DESNZ CGL.",
      "evidence": "5.4.2 Discontinuation risk for Padeswood"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Potential fraudulent claims or financial mismanagement in grant drawdowns and revenue support disbursement.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Implement Open Book Model cost assessments, independent financial assurance, and CGL grant compliance oversight.",
      "evidence": "5.4.4 Fraud"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Exchequer financial exposure under Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and Government Support Package variations during remediation.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Subject all variation requests and Government Support Package decisions to rigorous review by the Cluster Sponsor Function and SRO.",
      "evidence": "5.4.3 Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Underutilisation of the HyNet transport and storage network capacity if captured CO2 volumes fall short of projections.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Monitor unutilised capacity metrics and accelerate competitive selection for build-out users to maximize network utilisation.",
      "evidence": "Volume of unutilised network capacity (Mtpa) across the clusters by 2030"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Implementation of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) in 2027 may expose unabated domestic cement production if capture deployment slips.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Align project delivery milestones with 2027 CBAM timelines to ensure domestic decarbonised cement is market-ready.",
      "evidence": "The UK Carbon-Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)... will be introduced in 2027. However, unabated UK sites would be competing with sites overseas."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Shortages in specialized CCUS supply chain capacity and technical skills could delay construction and upskilling objectives.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Monitor supply chain spend, support regional workforce training, and track skill level metrics over the support contract lifespan.",
      "evidence": "Stimulate the CCUS supply chain, jobs, and skills, over the support contracts’ lifespans"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Operational reliance on external network operator T&SCo (Liverpool Bay) and economic regulation by Ofgem introduces third-party dependency risk.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Require strict adherence to the CCS Network Code and coordinate multi-party oversight through the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function.",
      "evidence": "Ofgem: Economic Regulator for T&S Network Users and T&SCo (Liverpool Bay)"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Integrating FOAK carbon capture technology at an operational cement plant at scale introduces potential technical integration and performance risks.
risks.mitigation: Conduct independent technical assurance via third-party experts and enforce strict performance thresholds within the Industrial Carbon Capture contract.
risks.evidence: Padeswood will be the first at-scale UK cement plant incorporating Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) technology

risks.description: Spurline development delays could force a 4-month delay to Final Investment Decision (FID) and a 5-month delay to Commercial Operation Date (COD).
risks.mitigation: Proactively align spurline delivery timelines and project FID milestones via the Cluster Sponsor Function oversight body.
risks.evidence: FID is delayed by 4 months to align with their spurline timelines, resulting in a subsequent 5-month delay to COD

risks.description: Rising carbon prices and exposure to unabated overseas competition risk carbon leakage and loss of market share prior to full CCUS operation.
risks.mitigation: Deploy Industrial Carbon Capture revenue support contracts to bridge the operating cost gap and maintain market competitiveness.
risks.evidence: Without CCUS, the cement industry will increasingly be exposed to a rising carbon price, impacting competitiveness with imports.

risks.description: Internationally owned corporate parent may de-prioritise UK interests and reallocate investment overseas if UK decarbonisation frameworks lag.
risks.mitigation: Provide long-term policy and commercial certainty through 25-year business model frameworks and Grant Funding Agreements.
risks.evidence: Most UK cement sites are operated by companies that are internationally owned and make investment decisions on a global basis.

risks.description: High upfront capital expenditure during capture facility construction creates risk of cost overruns and funding shortfalls.
risks.mitigation: Provide upfront capital support via the CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant up to 50% of eligible costs using an Open Book Model.
risks.evidence: The CCS Infrastructure Fund (CIF) Grant, which provides upfront capital support during the construction phase, up to 50% of Padeswood’s eligible capital costs.

risks.description: Interdependent cross-chain interfaces between the Padeswood capture plant and the broader HyNet T&S network create operational delivery risks.
risks.mitigation: Establish a dedicated Cluster Sponsor Function to actively manage cross-chain delivery and operating model integration risks.
risks.evidence: Managing government-owned cross-chain delivery risks and operating model integration risks.

risks.description: Fluctuations in captured CO2 volumes or operational disruptions create income uncertainty under long-term support contracts.
risks.mitigation: Structure revenue support under a Contract-for-Difference model tying payments to captured CO2 performance and volume thresholds.
risks.evidence: address key market barriers facing CCS deployment – such as high upfront costs, cross-chain risks, and revenue uncertainty

risks.description: Premature project discontinuation during development or operation could result in major write-downs of public capital and unfulfilled carbon targets.
risks.mitigation: Enforce Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and continuous compliance monitoring by LCCC and DESNZ CGL.

risks.description: Potential fraudulent claims or financial mismanagement in grant drawdowns and revenue support disbursement.
risks.mitigation: Implement Open Book Model cost assessments, independent financial assurance, and CGL grant compliance oversight.

risks.description: Exchequer financial exposure under Secretary of State Direct Agreements (SoSDA) and Government Support Package variations during remediation.
risks.mitigation: Subject all variation requests and Government Support Package decisions to rigorous review by the Cluster Sponsor Function and SRO.
risks.evidence: 5.4.3 Exchequer funding Secretary of State direct agreements (SoSDA)

risks.description: Underutilisation of the HyNet transport and storage network capacity if captured CO2 volumes fall short of projections.
risks.mitigation: Monitor unutilised capacity metrics and accelerate competitive selection for build-out users to maximize network utilisation.
risks.evidence: Volume of unutilised network capacity (Mtpa) across the clusters by 2030

risks.description: Implementation of the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) in 2027 may expose unabated domestic cement production if capture deployment slips.
risks.mitigation: Align project delivery milestones with 2027 CBAM timelines to ensure domestic decarbonised cement is market-ready.
risks.evidence: The UK Carbon-Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)... will be introduced in 2027. However, unabated UK sites would be competing with sites overseas.

risks.description: Shortages in specialized CCUS supply chain capacity and technical skills could delay construction and upskilling objectives.
risks.mitigation: Monitor supply chain spend, support regional workforce training, and track skill level metrics over the support contract lifespan.
risks.evidence: Stimulate the CCUS supply chain, jobs, and skills, over the support contracts’ lifespans

risks.description: Operational reliance on external network operator T&SCo (Liverpool Bay) and economic regulation by Ofgem introduces third-party dependency risk.
risks.mitigation: Require strict adherence to the CCS Network Code and coordinate multi-party oversight through the DESNZ Cluster Sponsor Function.
risks.evidence: Ofgem: Economic Regulator for T&S Network Users and T&SCo (Liverpool Bay)
